14B4.name: Scratch X low (platform/Bowser)
14B4.kind: scratch byte (low byte of a 16-bit word with $14B5)
desc: Shared scratch word, reused by unrelated bosses. In the rotating/tilting platform code it holds the X
position of a point being tested (sprite X low + 8 for the Iggy/Larry platform, tested by the Mode 7
rotated tile check; $14B5 is the high byte). In the Mode 7 boss room it is the contact X for Mario.
In the Bowser fight the same address is used as the Bowser phase counter (probably); set to the phase
in the Mario/Mecha-Koopa contact code and read by the state/music table.

14B5.name: Scratch X high / Bowser hurt timer
14B5.kind: scratch byte (high byte with $14B4), timer in Bowser fight
desc: High byte of the 16-bit point X in the platform geometry code ($14B4 is the low byte). Set to X high
plus carry for the Iggy/Larry tilting platform and by extended sprite hitbox setup.
In the Bowser fight it is the hurt/hit flash timer: set to $4C when Bowser is hit, read by the hurt
reaction and the main logic.

14B6.name: Scratch Y low / Bowser ball timer
14B6.kind: scratch byte (low byte of a 16-bit word with $14B7), timer in Bowser fight
desc: Low byte of the 16-bit point Y in the platform geometry code (sprite Y low + $2F for the Iggy/Larry
platform; $14B7 is the high byte). Also the contact Y in the Mode 7 boss room Mario test.
In the Bowser fight it is the ball throw timer: set by the attack scheduler, tested by the Mechakoopa
drop and ball throw routine, and cleared (STZ) when Bowser is hurt to cancel the throw.

14B7.name: Scratch Y high / falling object X
desc: High byte of the 16-bit point Y used by the platform geometry code ($14B6 is the low byte).
In Bowser state 1 (retreat off-screen) it holds the X start of the next falling object, a random
multiple of $10.

14B8.name: Platform X low / Bowser ball count
14B8.kind: scratch byte (low byte of a word with $14B9), counter in Bowser fight
desc: Low byte of the world X of a tilting/rotating platform: the brown chained platform, the Iggy/Larry
tilting platform (pivot X plus the rotated X offset) and the Mode 7 boss room contact test.
Iggy/Larry also keep the kid's X here for drawing the splash and spawning the ball.
In the Bowser fight it is the ball counter, incremented by the attack scheduler and read by the
Mechakoopa drop and ball throw routine.

14B9.name: Platform X high
desc: High byte of the world X of the platform being processed ($14B8 is the low byte). Written by the
brown chained platform main routine from the tile's 16-bit X, read by the Mario interaction helpers.

14BA.name: Platform Y low
14BA.kind: scratch byte (low byte of a word with $14BB)
desc: Low byte of the world Y of a tilting/rotating platform (pivot Y minus the rotated Y offset), also the
Iggy/Larry kid's Y position and the contact Y for the Mode 7 boss room Mario test (masked with $F0).
Read by the brown chained platform, Iggy's ball spawn, the platform Koopaling draw and splash draw.

14BB.name: Platform Y high
desc: High byte of the world Y of the platform being processed ($14BA is the low byte). Written by the
brown chained platform main routine, read by the Mario interaction helpers.

14BC.name: Rotation radius X
desc: X component of the offset from the pivot to a point on the rotating platform. Set to $50 by the
platform Mario interaction helper, or to point X [$14B4] minus pivot X by the rotated tile check.
Used with the sine/cosine magnitudes $14C2/$14C5 when rotating the offset by the platform angle.

14BF.name: Rotation radius Y
desc: Y component of the offset from the pivot to a point on the rotating platform. Set to 0 by the platform
Mario interaction helper, or to point Y [$14B6] minus pivot Y by the rotated tile check.
Companion of $14BC.

14C2.name: Sine magnitude (platform)
desc: Sine magnitude of the platform angle, looked up from the circle table (CircleCoords[angle & $FF]).
Written and read only inside the platform Mario interaction and geometry helpers.

14C5.name: Cosine magnitude (platform)
desc: Cosine magnitude of the platform angle, looked up from the same table as $14C2.
Written and read only inside the platform Mario interaction and geometry helpers.

14C8.name: Sprite status
14C8.kind: byte table, one per sprite slot (index X)
desc: The state of each sprite slot. Everything that spawns, kills or processes a sprite goes through it; the
main sprite loop dispatches on it each frame. Index Y is also used when one sprite acts on another.
Values: 0 = empty slot / erased; 1 = initialise; 2 = killed (falls off screen); 3 = smushed;
4 = spin-jump killed (puff of smoke); 5 = sinking in lava; 8 = normal (run main routine);
9 = carryable (stunned/shell or item); 0A = kicked; 0B = carried by Mario.

14D4.name: Sprite Y position high
14D4.kind: byte table, one per sprite slot (index X or Y)
desc: High byte of each sprite's 16-bit Y position; the low byte is $00D8 (RAM_SpriteYLo). Together they give
the sprite's position in the level. Written when sprites spawn, move or follow platforms and read for
collision, on-screen tests and drawing. $FE is used to park a sprite far off-screen (Bowser's clown car).

14E0.name: Sprite X position high
14E0.kind: byte table, one per sprite slot (index X or Y)
desc: High byte of each sprite's 16-bit X position; the low byte is $00E4 (RAM_SpriteXLo).
Written when sprites spawn and when they are carried by layers or Yoshi, read by the sprite-to-sprite
contact, interaction and draw code. New sprites copy the spawner's value.

14EC.name: Sprite Y sub-pixel fraction
14EC.kind: byte table, one per sprite slot (index X)
desc: Fractional part of a sprite's Y position, in 1/16 pixel units. The Y update routines add speed * 16
to it each frame and carry into the whole-pixel Y position. Cleared when the sprite tables are reset.

1504.name: Chained platform swing speed
1504.kind: byte table, one per sprite slot (index X)
desc: Angular speed of the brown swinging chained platform. Moves one step toward 0 each update (friction),
and Mario standing on it adds or subtracts 1 so his weight pumps the swing. Read when advancing the
angle. Cleared with the other per-sprite tables.

151C.name: Sprite misc table 1
151C.kind: byte table, one per sprite slot (index X)
desc: General-purpose per-sprite byte whose meaning depends on the sprite type. Examples: main state of the
Koopa Kids, Ludwig and Bowser; hop counter of the winged Goomba; Yoshi tongue length; burst expansion
rate of a firework; angle low of the brown chained platform; damping counter of the wall springboard;
angry flag of the Wiggler.

1528.name: Sprite misc table 2
1528.kind: byte table, one per sprite slot (index X)
desc: General-purpose per-sprite byte, meaning depends on the sprite type. Examples: phase counter of Dry
Bones, face state of the Thwomp, hit count of a Chuck, angle high of the brown chained platform (also
the Mode 7 rotated check), line table pointer high byte for line guides, animation frame of the Urchin.
For several platforms it holds the X movement since last frame, which carries Mario along.

1534.name: Sprite misc table 3
1534.kind: byte table, one per sprite slot (index X)
desc: General-purpose per-sprite byte, meaning depends on the sprite type (source label BlinkFallFlag).
Examples: bubble life timer, line guide step index, phase of the Diggin Chuck, collapsed flag of Dry
Bones, number of rockets launched in the fireworks, bob direction of clouds and the flying question
block (INC to reverse), window timer of the wall springboard, time counter of Iggy/Larry.

1540.name: Sprite timer 1
1540.kind: byte table, one per sprite slot (index X)
desc: General-purpose countdown timer for each sprite slot, the most used of the sprite timers. Sprites set
it to a frame count and the main routine counts it down by one per frame (when sprites are not locked)
and acts when it reaches zero.
Meaning is per sprite type: Dry Bones reassemble time, Bob-omb explosion timer ($40), Chuck charge
time ($20), Ludwig timer ($30), Mario-contact stun ($FF).
Values: 0 = timer expired / not running.

154C.name: Sprite interaction disable timer
154C.kind: byte table, one per sprite slot (index X)
desc: Countdown during which the sprite cannot touch Mario. Set after a stomp, bounce or kick (8 or $10
frames) so the same contact is not processed twice, after being hit by a bounce block, and by bosses
(Bowser $20, Iggy/Larry stun $18). Non-zero means skip Mario contact; the sprite routines count it down.
A few sprites reuse it as a plain wait timer (Bird turn delay, Keyhole, Bonus game flash).
Values: 0 = interaction enabled.

1558.name: Sprite timer 2
1558.kind: byte table, one per sprite slot (index X)
desc: General-purpose countdown timer, second of the sprite timers. Meaning is per sprite type: delay
before a shelless Koopa turns into a Koopa ($20), message box time, Lakitu throw timer, Podoboo wait
on the ground ($80), Monty Mole hop delay, Yoshi tongue pause (8), Ludwig timer ($60).
When non-zero in a pair of Koopas a kick or hop into the shell is in progress, so sprite-to-sprite
contact is skipped. Cleared (STZ) to cancel.

1564.name: Sprite timer 3
1564.kind: byte table, one per sprite slot (index X or Y)
desc: General-purpose countdown timer, third of the sprite timers. Often an intangibility or contact cooldown:
a non-zero value on either sprite stops sprite-to-sprite contact, and kicked sprites get 8 to briefly
ignore others. Also used as animation timers: Yoshi swallow timer ($1B), Bowser phase 9 animation
($12), Iggy/Larry shell animation ($7F), Urchin turning (8), firework scene end delay ($70).
Values: 0 = not running.

1570.name: Sprite misc table 4
1570.kind: byte table, one per sprite slot (index X)
desc: General-purpose per-sprite counter, meaning depends on the sprite type. Examples: wing flap counter of
the winged Goomba, walk counter of Dry Bones, Sumo Bro and Iggy/Larry, parachute sway index, hops left
of the bird, spawn count of the coin game cloud, burst size of a firework, segment length of line guides.
Usually incremented or decremented each frame by the sprite's main routine.

157C.name: Sprite facing direction
157C.kind: byte table, one per sprite slot (index X or Y)
desc: Which way each sprite faces and walks. Set when sprites spawn, turn at walls or face Mario, and read by
the draw routines to flip the graphics and by the movement code to pick the X speed.
Yoshi, Koopas, Rex, Wiggler and the Koopa Kids all use it. Briefly modified (XOR) by some draw routines.
Values: 0 = facing right; 1 = facing left.

1588.name: Sprite blocked-by-object flags
1588.kind: bit flags table, one per sprite slot (index X)
desc: Which sides of the sprite touched solid objects this frame, set by the sprite-block interaction and
map16 lookup routines and cleared (STZ) at the start of each check so it reverts to zero when the
sprite stops touching. Read by almost every walking or falling sprite to turn at walls, land on
the ground or hit the ceiling. Goal tape INCs it to flip direction.
Bits: 0 right wall; 1 left wall; 2 on ground; 3 hit ceiling (higher bits: layer 2 contact, probably).

1594.name: Sprite misc table 5
1594.kind: byte table, one per sprite slot (index X or Y)
desc: General-purpose per-sprite byte, meaning depends on the sprite type. Examples: Yoshi tongue state
(1 extending, 2 retracting), Mario-nearby flag of the Piranha Plant, slot of the sprite touched or of
the Hammer Bro on a platform, wall number for Morton/Roy, Chuck head scan step, bob direction of the
flying question block, hit height of the goal tape.

15A0.name: Sprite off-screen horizontal flag
15A0.kind: flag byte table, one per sprite slot (index X)
desc: Set by the get-sprite-draw-info routines (banks 1, 2 and 3) when any part of the sprite is outside the
screen horizontally. Read by the sprite main routines to skip actions and by the OAM drawers to set the
X high bit. Bosses clear it to make sure they never despawn.
Values: 0 = on screen horizontally; non-zero = off-screen.

15AC.name: Sprite turn-around timer
15AC.kind: byte table, one per sprite slot (index X or Y)
desc: Countdown for the turning animation when a sprite changes direction. Set to 8 by the flip-direction
routine and walking Koopas, to $10 for Yoshi and the Koopa Kids, and to $1F for Boo and Big Boo. The
draw routines read it to show the turn frame, and a non-zero value delays other behaviour.
Values: 0 = not turning.

15B8.name: Sprite slope steepness
15B8.kind: byte table, one per sprite slot (index X)
desc: Slope the sprite is standing on, written by the vertical map16 check and cleared when the sprite
leaves it. Used as a speed offset so sprites speed up going down a slope and slow going up (EOR with
the X speed to test direction), and by the slope movement and gravity routines.
Values: 0 = flat ground; non-zero = signed slope speed offset.

15C4.name: Sprite far off-screen flag
15C4.kind: flag byte table, one per sprite slot (index X)
desc: Set to 1 by the get-sprite-draw-info routines when the sprite is far off screen horizontally. Also set
for platforms when sprites are locked. When non-zero the OAM finish routine skips Mario interaction
and the Banzai Bill/platform code skips work.
Values: 0 = near the screen; 1 = far off-screen.

15D0.name: Sprite being eaten flag
15D0.kind: flag byte table, one per sprite slot (index X or Y)
desc: Set to 1 while Yoshi's tongue has a sprite and is swallowing it. Contact and interaction routines OR it
in so the sprite is ignored (bounce blocks, fireballs, sprite-to-sprite loop). Cleared when the sprite is
spat out. Magikoopa sets it while hidden (probably so Yoshi cannot eat it).
Values: 0 = not eaten; non-zero = on Yoshi's tongue.

15DC.name: Sprite contact/ledge flag
15DC.kind: byte table, one per sprite slot (index X or Y)
desc: Little-used per-sprite flag. The Moving ledge (hole) sprite clears it ($0 = no contact) and the
gravity update routine reads it. Cleared by the per-sprite table reset.
Exact meaning is probably a contact flag; only seen as set/cleared and tested once.

15E9.name: Current sprite slot
desc: Slot number of the sprite whose routine is running. The main sprite loop stores X here before calling
each sprite, and subroutines reload X from it after they have trashed X (draw routines, extended
sprite code, the spawn routines). Also compared against other slots to skip a sprite's own slot.

15EA.name: Sprite OAM index
15EA.kind: byte table, one per sprite slot (index X)
desc: Byte offset into the OAM buffer where this sprite's tiles are written. The slot assigner gives each
sprite its offset and sprite draw routines load Y from it. Some sprites add 4 per tile to move to the
next OAM slot, or set 0 to take the first OAM slots (draw priority).

15F6.name: Sprite palette and properties
15F6.kind: byte table, one per sprite slot (index X or Y); YXPPCCCT
desc: OAM property byte for the sprite: palette, priority and flips. Loaded from the sprite tweaker table when
the sprite spawns and ORed into the tile properties by the draw routines.
Bits: 7 Y flip; 6 X flip; 4-5 priority; 1-3 palette; 0 name table. Cheep Cheep and the killed-sprite code
shift bit 7 out (clears Y flip); the Bob-omb flashes by EORing in ([$1540] * 2) & $0E.

1602.name: Sprite animation frame
1602.kind: byte table, one per sprite slot (index X)
desc: Current graphics frame of the sprite. The main routine picks it (from a frame table or by counting) and
the draw routine selects the tiles from it. Examples: Yoshi frame, Chuck frame, Boo face visible (0) or
hiding (3), springboard frame, walk frame of Ludwig and Iggy/Larry.
The flying grey turnblocks reuse it as a direction switch timer.

160E.name: Sprite misc table 6
160E.kind: byte table, one per sprite slot (index X or Y)
desc: General-purpose per-sprite byte, meaning depends on the sprite type. Examples: for Yoshi, slot of the
sprite held in his mouth ($FF = none); for a shelless Koopa, slot of the sprite to kick; Mario-on-platform
flag for Banzai Bill chained platforms; Lakitu slot for the cloud; Chuck jump flag; Morton/Roy right
walk limit; goal tape hit flag; current line guide segment number.

161A.name: Sprite index in level data
161A.kind: byte table, one per sprite slot (index X)
desc: Index of this sprite in the level's sprite list, set when the sprite is spawned from the level data so
it is not respawned while on screen and can be marked as spawned again when erased.
Values: $FF = never reload this sprite (erased permanently, or a group spawn that should respawn only
through its leader).

1626.name: Sprite misc counter
1626.kind: byte table, one per sprite slot (index X or Y)
desc: Per-sprite counter. For ordinary sprites it counts consecutive kills made by a kicked shell or stomps
(kill chain), added into the points given and cleared when Mario lands. Also Ludwig and Koopa Kid hit
counts. Line-guided platforms use it as a waiting-for-Mario flag (probably). Cleared by the table reset.

1632.name: Sprite behind-scenery flag
1632.kind: flag byte table, one per sprite slot (index X or Y)
desc: Which layer the sprite is on: in front of or behind layer 1 scenery. Sprites only interact when both
have the same value, so it is EORed in contact checks. Net Koopas toggle it when climbing through a net,
and the pipe Lakitu sets it to go behind scenery. Read by the draw routines for priority.
Values: 0 = in front; non-zero = behind scenery.

163E.name: Sprite timer 4
163E.kind: byte table, one per sprite slot (index X or Y)
desc: General-purpose countdown timer, fourth of the sprite timers. Meaning is per sprite type: Pipe Lakitu
hold timer, P-switch pressed timer, Iggy/Larry defeat timer ($50), Urchin ($0C), kick animation of a
shelless Koopa ($20), draw priority timer of the flying question block ($50).
Values: 0 = not running. Some tests use bit 7 as negative.

164A.name: Sprite in-liquid flags
164A.kind: bit flags table, one per sprite slot (index X or Y)
desc: Set by the sprite-block interaction each frame when the sprite is inside water or lava, then cleared
and recomputed next frame. The gravity routine reads it to use slow-sink physics and sprites inherit it
when spawned (shelless Koopa from shell). Rip Van Fish sets it in init.
Bits: 0 water; 7 lava. Morton/Roy, Ludwig and Bowser reuse it as a plain timer or flag.

1656.name: Sprite tweaker byte 1
1656.kind: bit flags table, one per sprite slot (index X or Y); sSjJcccc
desc: Per-sprite behaviour flags, copied from the Sprite1656Vals table by sprite number at spawn. Read by the
stomp, bounce and kill routines.
Bits: 7 disappear in a puff of smoke when killed; 6 can hop into/kick shells; 5 dies (smushed) when
jumped on; 4 can be jumped on; 0-3 object clipping index (which hitbox shape is used).
Bob-omb explosion clears the byte so the sprite cannot be stomped.
